proxy_language: Proto-Algonquian (reconstructed, with Proto-Siouan and Proto-Iroquoian as alternates for texture)
proxy_rationale: The Early Archaic (c. 10,000-8,000 BP) of the Eastern Woodlands predates any attested language by 8,000+ years, and no linguistic continuity can be demonstrated. Proto-Algonquian (c. 2,500-3,000 BP, northern/eastern origin) is the best-reconstructed language family of the broad region and gives a real, rule-governed morphology (Bloomfield 1946; Goddard; Aubin's Proto-Algonquian dictionary). The link to Early Archaic peoples is purely areal and entirely speculative; names should be read as a stylised Eastern Woodlands flavour, not as the actual language of these foragers.
phonology: Proto-Algonquian (Bloomfield/Goddard notation) consonants: *p *t *c (affricate, ch) *k *s *sh (esh) *th (eth-like) *l *m *n *w *y *h plus *? as cluster member; long and short vowels *i *o *a *e and long *ii *oo *aa *ee. No voicing contrast in stops, no /f r b d g/. Cluster-internal *x (unknown fricative) and *? occur only in clusters.
phonotactics: Syllables are (C)V(:) with medial clusters of the type *hC (preaspirated: *hp *ht *hk *hc *hs *hsh *hth *hl *hm *hn) and *?C, plus *C + *w or *y glide (*kw *pw *mw *hkw). Words end in a vowel or in a suffixed consonant (-w, -k, -n, -l, -a, -ki, -ar). No word-initial clusters, no word-initial *h-clusters, no consonant-final stems in roots except via inflection. Preaspirated clusters and vowel length matter for spelling; stress is not written.
orthography: Use plain-Latin Proto-Algonquian-style transliteration: sh for esh, th for eth, c written as ch for the game, long vowels doubled (aa ee ii oo), glottal stop as an apostrophe, preaspiration as h before a stop (ahp, ehk, ahs). Reconstructed forms carry an asterisk in the notes but names are written without asterisks. Final -w/-wa/-ki/-ni suffixes mark animate forms and plurals (-ak, -ar, -ni; Proto-Algonquian *-ki/-ahki locative).
morphology: Polysynthetic, head-final noun stems with an animate/inanimate gender split. Nouns are built from a root plus a final (abstract or concrete: *-aahkwa ~ tree/wood, *-aakani ~ instrument, *-ahsi ~ stone, *-wi ~ water). Initials and medials combine into stems; possession uses person prefixes (ne- 1, ke- 2, we- 3). Plurals: animate *-ak, inanimate *-ar. Locative *-ink / *-ing.
compounding: Compounds are initial + (medial) + final, head-final: [qualifier root]-[body final]. 'X of Y' is typically expressed by a possessed noun with we- (e.g. wi-) prefix, or a noun with locative -enk/-ink; 'Y-maker' is built from a verb root plus a nominalizing final (*-aakani instrument, *-iwa agent). There is no genitive case marker on the possessor; ordering is possessor + possessed with prefix on the head.
noun_phrase_order: Modifier before head (adjectival or numeral initial + noun final), possessor before possessed; demonstratives precede; locatives are suffixed to the noun.

worked_examples.name: Nipaawi meneka
worked_examples.gloss: nip-aawi water-final + menek- stew/cook (illustrative stylised formation)

sources: Bloomfield, Leonard. 'Algonquian' in Linguistic Structures of Native America, 1946
Goddard, Ives. 'The Algonquian Languages' in Handbook of North American Indians vol. 17, 1996
Aubin, George F. A Proto-Algonquian Dictionary, 1975
Siebert, Frank. 'Resurrecting Virginia Algonquian from the Dead' in Studies in Southeastern Indian Languages, 1975
notes: Entirely speculative proxy: the Early Archaic has no linguistic evidence and Proto-Algonquian postdates it by millennia; the family is also not the only candidate in the region (Siouan, Iroquoian, Muskogean, and now-extinct isolates were all present). Some listed roots are approximations of Proto-Algonquian shapes; verify each against Aubin/Wiktionary before shipping. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word since the language is not Goidelic. Avoid repeating current game strings (apostrophe-heavy or 'x'-containing forms like Yiwihon, Hit'o, Kosatho thiyoxsoch), which do not match Algonquian phonotactics.
